title: URL SHORTENER
premise: A short link moves through an edge, cache, database, and queue before analytics catches up.
audiencePromise: See how redirects stay focused while click data takes a separate path.
openLoop: What keeps every short-link click from reaching the database?
payoff: Caching handles lookups, while queued clicks become warehouse data separately.
engagementQuestion: Would you choose cached redirects with queued analytics, or direct analytics writes?

scenes.headline: WHO REACHES THE DATABASE?
scenes.narration: What keeps every short-link click from reaching the database?
scenes.caption: The database is not first

scenes.headline: THE REQUEST’S FIRST STOPS
scenes.narration: The Visitor meets the CDN edge first; the Link API, Redis cache, and Postgres wait inside the Private network.
scenes.caption: Outside first, private inside

scenes.headline: ANALYTICS HAS ITS OWN LANE
scenes.narration: New links use the Link API, while the Click queue sends click records toward the Analytics warehouse.
scenes.caption: Writes split from redirects

scenes.headline: START AT THE EDGE
scenes.narration: The Visitor opens a short link, and the CDN edge checks whether it can answer without forwarding the request.
scenes.caption: The edge gets first chance

scenes.headline: MISS, THEN FORWARD
scenes.narration: On an edge miss, the CDN edge forwards the request to the Link API inside the Private network.
scenes.caption: Only misses go deeper

scenes.headline: CACHE BEFORE DATABASE
scenes.narration: The Link API looks up the code in the Redis cache; a cache miss sends the read to Postgres.
scenes.caption: The cache shields the database

scenes.headline: SAVE THE NEW LINK
scenes.narration: For a new link, the Link API saves the link in Postgres.
scenes.caption: The destination is persisted

scenes.headline: QUEUE THE CLICK
scenes.narration: After the click, the Link API logs it through the Click queue, separating click work from the link lookup.
scenes.caption: Click work waits separately

scenes.headline: BATCH FOR ANALYTICS
scenes.narration: The Click queue batches those records into the Analytics warehouse, where the write flow becomes analytics data.
scenes.caption: The warehouse receives batches

scenes.headline: TWO JOBS, TWO PATHS
scenes.narration: The design keeps lookup layers separate from queued analytics, so redirecting and reporting do not share one write path.
scenes.caption: Redirects and reporting diverge

scenes.headline: CACHE OR SIMPLICITY?
scenes.narration: Would you choose cached redirects with queued analytics, or a simpler path that writes analytics directly?
scenes.caption: Which tradeoff would you take?
